text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Confirm and classify the diagnosis: MRI of the brain and the cervical and thoracic spine with gadolinium to the MAGNIMS-CMSC-NAIMS protocol, read against the 1971 McDonald criteria; exclude mimics with vitamin B12, TSH and HIV; request the records of the original evaluation
  • Neurology (multiple sclerosis) consultation to confirm and classify the disease and advise on disease-modifying therapy, its monitoring, vaccination, symptom care and MRI follow-up
  • Screening before any disease-modifying therapy: hepatitis B surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody; quantitative immunoglobulins; liver tests; blood count with lymphocytes; varicella and measles immunity; tuberculosis blood test; HIV and hepatitis C; JC virus antibody; and vaccines brought up to date, inactivated vaccines at least two weeks and live vaccines at least four weeks before the first dose
  • Relapse and pseudo-relapse plan: new or worsening symptoms lasting more than 24 hours without fever or heat mean a same-day call; check for urinary infection and fever first, because infection and heat can bring back old symptoms; written card for her bag
  • Mobility, spasticity and falls: physical therapy evaluation for gait, strengthening, stretching, balance and a home exercise program; review of walking aids, with forearm crutches or a rollator and a scooter for long distances when she wants them; home safety review; daily stretching
  • Bladder: post-void residual today, timed voiding, fluids earlier in the day, less caffeine, pelvic floor exercises, and a medicine if urgency persists; urine check for any burning, fever or sudden worsening
  • Fatigue and heat sensitivity: energy conservation and pacing with an occupational therapy review, teaching sessions placed in the morning where she chooses, cooling garments, air conditioning, cool drinks, and aerobic exercise such as pool exercise in cool water
  • Work: a letter to her employer, with her consent, describing her functional needs (an accessible teaching room near an elevator, a chair and lectern for lectures, reserved parking near her building, and flexibility for medical appointments) without naming the diagnosis; she decides what to disclose
  • Bone health: vitamin D3 with a recheck, calcium from food, weight-bearing exercise, fall prevention, and bone density at the preventive visit because of reduced mobility and earlier steroid courses
  • Mood and cognition: PHQ-9 at intake and every six months; ask about concentration and word-finding; counseling offered at any time
  • On the consultant's advice: ocrelizumab 300 mg on day 1 and day 15 and then 600 mg every 6 months, after the vaccines and at least two weeks after the last inactivated dose, with premedication and observation; blood count and immunoglobulins before each dose; a re-baseline brain MRI three to six months after the first dose and then yearly; baclofen titrated to 10 mg three times a day; mirabegron with a blood pressure check at each visit

resource.description: Primary care, coordinated with a multiple sclerosis neurologist, for a 44-year-old professor and public speaker who walks with a cane and has multiple sclerosis diagnosed elsewhere: confirming and classifying the disease with MRI of the brain and spine under the 1971 McDonald criteria and the 1975 MAGNIMS-CMSC-NAIMS consensus, choosing a disease-modifying therapy by course and risk under the AAN 1972 guideline, the screening and vaccination it needs before the first dose (hepatitis B serology, immunoglobulins, liver tests, blood counts, varicella and measles immunity, tuberculosis, inactivated vaccines at least two weeks ahead), its monitoring afterwards, a re-baseline MRI, recognizing relapse and pseudo-relapse, symptom care for spasticity, bladder, fatigue and heat sensitivity, mobility equipment and fall prevention, a workplace accommodation that discloses only what she chooses, bone health, mood screening, and preventive care, respecting her wish to keep her diagnosis private.
